synthesis: The symmetry conditions defining HP do more than shrink the ambient Hilbert space: folding the weighted norm and multiplying by the sine factor identify HP isometrically with the odd-cosine Fourier sector, where the adjacent sine differences E_p are a complete orthonormal basis. The coefficient-correction argument then shows that replacing the ambient fractional-part generators by e_q={qt}-{t} preserves the RH closure criterion, and the coordinate formula <E_p,e_q>=log q-sum_{p/q<=k<p}1/k turns that closure problem into convergence of explicit arithmetic coordinate sequences.
source_support: Unit u02 constructs the orthonormal E_p family and identifies the two symmetries of HP; u03 proves completeness by the norm-preserving Fourier representation; u05 quantitatively controls the coefficient sum needed to transfer the ambient Nyman-Beurling approximation into HP; and u06 computes the resulting basis coordinates as a logarithm minus a finite harmonic interval.
nonparaphrase_operation: Composes a symmetry-selected isometry, a controlled generator-family correction, and an exact coordinate extraction to explain why a function-space RH closure criterion becomes an arithmetic sequence approximation problem.
limits: The equivalence depends on the proved correction of the symmetry-violating component and does not justify arbitrary subspace restriction. Exact multiplier, integral-normalization, and endpoint formulas carry OCR risk, and the coordinate identity alone does not establish convergence.
quality_reason: Accepted because the computational reduction requires the distinct mechanisms in u03, u05, and u06, with u02 supplying the basis/subspace boundary; no single parent yields the full reduction.

synthesis: The triangular, natural, and smoothed constructions all separate local coordinate correctness from global Hilbert-norm control. Boundary-corrected coefficients make the first n errors vanish exactly, while the natural and smoothed coefficients converge to the target in each fixed coordinate; each construction also controls sufficiently far-out coordinates. What remains is possible norm mass in a moving finite or low-frequency block, so a common square-summable dominator on that block is the additional burden rather than a consequence of coordinatewise convergence.
source_support: Unit u08 proves exact cancellation through coordinate n and leaves a tail beginning at n+1; u09 bounds the far triangular tail beyond n^4 and displays the intermediate window; u10 proves fixed-coordinate limits and far-tail decay for the natural coefficients while expressing the low-mode mass through two restrictive Moebius sums; and u11 preserves the fixed-coordinate limits and far-tail estimate after smoothing but still states a square-summable domination hypothesis.
nonparaphrase_operation: Aligns three different approximation schemes by the same fixed/intermediate/far-tail decomposition and locates the common missing norm-control obligation despite their different coefficient choices.
limits: Fixed-coordinate convergence never implies Hilbert-space convergence by itself. The frozen u09 span cuts off Criterion 1 before its quantifier and conclusion, so no RH implication for the triangular condition is certified from that unit alone; the domination hypotheses in u10 and u11 remain unproved.
quality_reason: Accepted because the shared obstruction emerges only by comparing the exact cancellation and tail localization in u08-u09 with the low-mode and smoothed analyses in u10-u11, not from a generic thematic overlap.

synthesis: The three coefficient designs exchange exact local cancellation for simpler arithmetic structure and then for stronger truncation regularity. Two terminal corrections added to Moebius-weighted interior coefficients solve the finite triangular system exactly; removing those corrections gives the natural mu(q)/q family but exposes a moving low-mode norm governed by two simultaneous summatory-Moebius conditions; multiplying by q^{-epsilon_n} introduces a vanishing fixed-coordinate bias while making the omitted Dirichlet tails directly controllable. Smoothing repairs tail estimation, not the remaining uniform Hilbert-norm domination problem.
source_support: Unit u08 derives the boundary-corrected coefficients from two scalar equations and annihilates the initial coordinates; u10 analyzes the pure mu(q)/q coefficients, obtains coordinatewise and far-tail control, and isolates two restrictive low-mode sums; u11 adds the vanishing exponent, estimates the omitted tails directly, and retains an explicit square-summable domination assumption.
nonparaphrase_operation: Compares the algebraic jobs performed by boundary correction, coefficient simplification, and exponent damping, showing precisely which error component each modification controls and which global burden survives.
limits: The exact artifacts do not support the candidate limit's reference to an improved conditional rate: u11 ends as the Balazard result begins. Only the sufficient smoothed criterion and its unresolved domination hypothesis are available; epsilon glyphs, terminal coefficient formulas, and the low-mode identity are formula-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted because the core tradeoff is concretely supported across u08, u10, and u11 and cannot be recovered from any one unit; the unsupported conditional-rate phrase is explicitly removed rather than propagated.
